bull.t: Strong Revenue Growth and Contracted Backlog
bull.b: Rapid year-over-year growth and a sizable signed server agreement indicate improving commercial traction and customer demand. If conversions proceed, the committed backlog can support revenue visibility, strengthen market credibility, and provide a foundation for scaling the edge-AI platform.

Blaize is building more than a single hardware product, combining OEM design wins with platform and service opportunities. This model could broaden customer reach, create repeatable solutions across verticals, and improve revenue durability as software and services expand.

bull.t: Low Leverage and Balance Sheet Repair
bull.b: Minimal debt reduces refinancing and interest-rate pressure, while the return to positive equity suggests meaningful balance-sheet repair. This gives management more flexibility to pursue operations and product development, although durable improvement still depends on reducing losses and cash consumption.

bear.t: Severe Losses and Persistent Cash Burn
bear.b: Large operating losses and sustained negative free cash flow weaken financial self-sufficiency and can force continued reliance on equity, financing, or customer advances. Persistent cash consumption limits investment flexibility and makes execution more vulnerable if growth takes longer to convert.

bear.t: Sharp Guidance Cut and Margin Compression
bear.b: The major outlook reduction shows that expected demand and customer conversions have not translated into revenue on schedule. Severe gross-margin compression, partly from lower-margin server hardware, also weakens the path to profitability and raises questions about earnings quality.

Regulatory investigations, litigation, and delayed customer payments create durable uncertainty around contracts, collections, and management bandwidth. These issues can impair cash conversion, increase costs, and make future customer commitments harder to secure while outcomes remain unresolved.
